actual_scope: A reusable toolkit of our stable, verified P104 tools for the hosted-word format of #7546 and later: (A) the exact pricer pricekit.py; (B) the frame-perp duality dualword.py (word -> dual word, a price-preserving involution); (C) the token-settled drop engine tokdrop.py (clean-mode stay-drop repair, premix settlement rank, exact build), which rebuilds our #7601 word byte-for-byte and, run on the dual, finds the main-902 drop; (D) checkers accx.py (fast randomised-exact replay with exact re-checks), lossless.py (law DUAL for lossy CLEARs), nativeplan.py (helper-plan extractor) and validate.py (accx + lossless + the repository's invoice tools); (E) pricing models kformula.py (closed-form caller C(k) and the kappa(k) law), layout_price.py and cap_check.py. Every tool ships with a runnable example and tests with positive and negative controls on vendored #7546 data.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a constructive helper-basis or causal-split improvement. This package instead ships the tools we used for such edits (drop repair and settlement, duality, exact checking and pricing), so others can run and extend them; it makes no kappa claim.
bottleneck_link: Every candidate P104 edit has to be repaired, settled, checked and priced exactly before it can be judged against the complete invoice; these tools do each step exactly and quickly on the current word format.
stop_rule: Every tool has docs, a CLI or API example and a test with positive and negative controls that runs in minutes on vendored data; claims are tagged; WIP tools are excluded; validator PASS.
evidence: README.md, pricekit.py, dualword.py, tokdrop.py, modp.py, accx.py, fastreplay.py, lossless.py, nativeplan.py, validate.py, kformula.py, layout_price.py, cap_check.py, sl_lib.py, tests/, data/, VERIFY.json.

open_questions.question: Do the remaining non-owned stays of the dual of #7546 (about 4,500, untried) or of the current frontier word hold more rank-0 drops?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The dual scan found a free drop (main 902 at chart 595) that no primal scan could see; each such drop is worth about +0.008% on its own.
open_questions.first_step: Run tokdrop.py scan over the dual's census (Context.census(), kinds without OW/OR), in shards; build every rank-0/0 hit with build_exact and map it back with dualword.py.
open_questions.blocked_by: CPU time only (about 10-30 s per stay).

open_questions.question: Can tier-A-only settlements (rank 0 with V-helper rows relaxed, rank >= 1 exactly) be made exact?
open_questions.why_it_matters: About ten such stays exist on #7546 and its dual (624@117, 627@117, 490@594 primal; 438@245, 271@306, 1289@117 dual); together worth up to ~7.7 D0 per call.
open_questions.first_step: For one stay, add the V-helper post-op freedom to the exact premix solve in build_exact and test whether the failing column becomes solvable.

open_questions.question: Is there a caller whose stages meet in bounded headers stitched by tree nodes, so that D_caller = O(k)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: kformula.py shows kappa(k) ~ eps/(beta ln k) -> 0 for every nested two-arm root; bounded top-field rank is the only route to a positive limit.
open_questions.first_step: Price a toy 8-stage caller with two bounded headers joined by one tree node with layout_price.py and check its crossings with cap_check.py.
